title: CINETRA: A Multi-Vendor Audit of Semantic Concept Transfer in Cardiac MRI (code, protocol and frozen results)

description:
CINETRA (cine semantic transition) audits what a frozen cardiac MRI classifier encodes, in the quantities a reader measures: ventricular volumes, ejection fractions and myocardial mass. A typed linear transition maps the classifier's 57 mask descriptors to measured concepts; variable-precision rough-set rules on the concepts must pass a cross-fitted gate before they may label a case; and every case receives one reason-coded route, a label or a computational abstention. The audit was registered as a signed protocol (CMR-TRANS-AUDIT 6.0.0 and its 6.0.1 amendment), frozen, and evaluated once on three public cohorts (ACDC, M&Ms-1 and M&Ms-2), one of them held out and unread until the registration.

This archive is the study's public record: the code that produced the results (byte-identical to the registered commit), the protocol and a verifiable proof of its registration, the aggregate results of the frozen run, the objects fitted on the ACDC development set, the figures, and tools to verify the registration and the datasets and to compare a re-run with the frozen results. It contains no image, mask or case-level data of the datasets, which must be obtained from their organizers. The accompanying article is in preparation. Research software, not for clinical use.
